input.title: The Lost Princess (Ma'aseh Me'Aveidat Bat Melech) — first of Rebbe Nachman's Sipurei Ma'asiyot
input.text_summary: A king has six sons and one beloved daughter. In a moment of anger he cries out, "may the Evil One take you" — and that very night she is gone, swallowed into exile. The king regrets bitterly and sends his most faithful minister to find and redeem her. The minister searches for years, refusing all comfort, sustained only by his faith that she can still be found. Along the way he gives charity, prays, and follows fading hints toward her. The tale (as Rebbe Nachman told it) breaks off before the ending — the minister has not yet redeemed her when the story stops, with the promise that the final redemption will unfold the same way.

sequence.phrase: a king had a beloved, only daughter
in a moment of anger he banishes her — she becomes an aveidah, a lost thing, swallowed into a place with no way back
the one sent to find her weeps through the long search
he is sustained only by unwavering faith that she can still be found
he gives charity along the way, as the seeking itself becomes an act of kindness
the yearning is poured out as prayer
the tale reaches toward redemption — and there the storyteller breaks off, unresolved

process_notes: Beats were distilled from the story's plot arc, then each resolved to a concept id via tmap.py search/match. Several thematically "obvious" picks (e.g. the princess-as-Shechinah motif, the wildman-guide, the bow of true desire) turned out to be low-degree leaf nodes in the graph with no attested causal (eitza) edge to their neighbors — the graph correctly refused to project them, per the map's own discipline: shared meaning is not a graph connection. The 7-concept sequence actually used here was rebuilt around concepts verified pairwise-connected in the correct causal direction (eitza edges are directed; reversing an attested pair breaks the projection). scripts/segment_project.py's DP then split it into 3 contiguous single-teaching segments — the 2-6 concept limit on a single project() call forces at least one cut, and the algorithm found the cut points that minimize total cost, correctly recognizing that the second cut (between faith and charity) costs nothing extra because both halves land in the same teaching (LM I:7) anyway — only the first cut is a real cross-teaching jump (LM I:10 → I:7).
narrative_by_segment: The king and the loss open in LM I:10 (cost 1.12) — the teaching where kingship's own wrath and its most drastic consequence, a lost/forgotten thing (aveidah), sit together. This is the very Hebrew word the story is named for.
Tears and faith close together in LM I:7 (cost 0.52) — a teaching whose causal spine runs from truth (emet) into faith (emunah), the exact resource the search draws on.

Charity, prayer, and the reach toward redemption land in the same teaching, LM I:7 (cost 0.64) — so the bridge from segment 2 to segment 3 is free: the story never actually leaves this teaching's world, it's only the 2-6 concept cap on one projection call that forced the cut.
narrative: The whole arc — loss, weeping, faith, charity, prayer, and the unfinished reach toward redemption — is attested almost entirely inside one teaching, Likutey Moharan I:7, with only one real jump: from the opening scene of a king's wrath and his lost daughter (LM I:10) into the sustained search (LM I:7). That single cross-teaching hop costs 2.5 in this model's terms — real, but small next to the six-fold richness of what's attested once you're inside I:7 itself: there, the map's own words state "אֵין אֱמוּנָה בְּלֹא אֱמֶת" — there is no faith without truth — and separately identifies exile's cure with truth, faith, and prayer in a single line ('by tzitzit one can come to the tzaddikim's counsel, to the aspect of truth; and through truth one comes to faith'). That is, when asked what could precede the minister's faith, the map's own attested edges (not an invented reading) answer: truth. And when asked what could precede the reach toward redemption, the same teaching answers: faith. The story never gives the ending — the minister has not yet found her when Rebbe Nachman breaks off — and the graph mirrors this exactly: c:ge-ulah-redemption has zero outgoing (effect) edges in the whole corpus. There is nothing attested as coming AFTER redemption in this teaching; the chain simply stops there, same as the tale itself, with the traditional coda: 'and so it will be with the final redemption.'
